column2: agreed merge:prosperar, but 93% capitalised and one example is a brand (Prospera massager); also could be próspera (adj. without accent): verb, adjective or brand?
agreed merge:mesías, but the only example is an English name ("YAHUSHUA Messiah"); a non-Spanish token whose Spanish reading is a minority drops
agreed merge:cuscús as first half of split loan "cous cous", but both halves are the same token "cous": merging all occurrences counts each "cous cous" twice
agreed merge:afroamericana: target is the feminine form; the adjective lemma is presumably afroamericano (cf. judeo-cristiana -> judeocristiano)
agreed merge:restaurar with no examples; 93% capitalised (Restaura), may be a brand or company name
agreed drop as brand, but may hide máxima (feminine of máximo / noun "maxim") written without accent
agreed drop as foreign, but it is a currency (Afghan afgani); earlier rulings keep currency names (rand, leu, birr kept here)
agreed keep as UN Volunteers; is a minor UN programme a famous international body under the institutions rule?
agreed keep as UN observer force (UNDOF); specialised UN mission, is it famous?
agreed keep as national research body; specialised public body, nationally famous?
agreed keep, but the spelling rule merges hyphenated spellings of a word Spanish writes as one (musculoesquelético)
agreed keep, but the written form is check-in; English spelling merge under the spellings rule?
